about: A Colossal Cave-style cave crawl. You pick up a lantern and sword in a barrow and cross a ravine to a cavern with a wizard. Beyond are a formal garden and a spinning carousel room. Treasures lie south, behind a stone door and a room that will not keep still.

done.why: After about 12 turns I hit an eight-passage spinning maze with no clear goal pulling me on. It looked like a slog, and I only give a few minutes.

moments.note: The wizard appears, zaps me weak, and I drop the lamp. Then he hints at where the treasure is.
Went south into pitch black with no warning that I needed the lamp lit. The grue line is a familiar jolt.
The garden with its topiary and a unicorn bounding off is a nice image. The unicorn's leaving also restores my energy.
The Carousel Room is an eight-exit spinning maze. I took it as a signal to quit.

wished: A clearer first goal, not just wandering.
Some sign of what the wizard's hints meant, or a quicker way to the pearls.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: It gave me a goal and a hint, the only real pull in the session.

lines.line: Eight identical passages leave the room.
lines.why: This is where I lost interest.

fun.why: Pleasant but familiar. I never hit a puzzle or an exciting moment before I quit.

engagement.why: The wizard hint briefly hooked me, then the walking and the maze lost me.

difficulty.why: Nothing blocked me in the short time I played. The maze looked like it would get hard.

interestingness.why: The wizard's knowing hints and the topiary were nice touches on a familiar cave.

prose.why: Clean, evocative room descriptions, and the wizard and carousel text had some personality.
